intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1A) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (NR3C2; 600983) on chromosome 4q31.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1A) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene NR3C2.
checks.evidence_quote: PCR and direct sequencing of the MR gene identified a heterozygous point mutation changing codon 924 Leu (CTG) to CCG (Pro) (L924P) in all affected members.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a dominant family with renal PHA1 that carries a heterozygous MR mutation. It concludes that the mineralocorticoid resistance is due to the MR mutation.

checks.claim: The mineralocorticoid receptor gene NR3C2 is located on chromosome 4q31.
checks.evidence_quote: we have screened the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (MLR) for variants
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene named in the paper; the abstract itself does not state 4q31.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I is a form of mineralocorticoid resistance that affects only the kidney. In the neonatal period it causes renal salt wasting, dehydration, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis, even though plasma renin activity and aldosterone are markedly raised. It is milder than the autosomal recessive multisystem form and usually improves with age. Sodium supplementation can often be stopped in childhood, and some adult carriers have no symptoms apart from high aldosterone levels.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I is a form of mineralocorticoid resistance that affects only the kidney.
checks.evidence_quote: we conclude that type I PHA includes two clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects
checks.explanation: Dominant kindred I had renal salt wasting; the conclusion distinguishes a renal form from a multi-organ form.

checks.claim: In the neonatal period, autosomal dominant PHA I causes renal salt wasting.
checks.evidence_quote: the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy (vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia)
checks.explanation: Renal salt wasting in infancy in the dominant kindred.

checks.claim: In the neonatal period, autosomal dominant PHA I causes dehydration.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Only the title was supplied, and it does not mention dehydration.

checks.claim: In the neonatal period, autosomal dominant PHA I causes hyperkalemia.
checks.evidence_quote: the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy (vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia)
checks.explanation: Hyperkalemia is listed.

checks.claim: In the neonatal period, autosomal dominant PHA I causes metabolic acidosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Only the title was supplied, and it does not mention metabolic acidosis.

checks.claim: In autosomal dominant PHA I, plasma renin activity is markedly raised.
checks.evidence_quote: hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr; however, the PRA decreased gradually to near normal values
checks.explanation: This implies renin was raised at first, but the abstract does not say it was 'markedly' raised, and it later fell to near normal.

checks.claim: In autosomal dominant PHA I, plasma aldosterone is markedly raised.
checks.evidence_quote: In affected members (propositus, mother, and two brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr
checks.explanation: Hyperaldosteronism is documented.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant PHA I is milder than the autosomal recessive multisystem form of PHA I.
checks.evidence_quote: clinical expression of PHA varied from asymptomatic to moderate
checks.explanation: The dominant kindred was asymptomatic to moderate and the recessive case was severe. The paper implies this comparison but does not state it as a general rule.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant PHA I usually improves with age.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is a milder disease that remits with age.
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: In autosomal dominant PHA I, sodium supplementation can often be stopped in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Sodium supplementation was discontinued at the age of two.
checks.explanation: This is shown for one propositus only; 'often' is a generalisation.

checks.claim: Some adult carriers of autosomal dominant PHA I have no symptoms apart from high aldosterone levels.
checks.evidence_quote: In seven additional family members from three generations, clinical expression of PHA varied from asymptomatic to moderate. In affected members (propositus, mother, and two brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr
checks.explanation: Asymptomatic affected relatives and persistent hyperaldosteronism are reported, but the abstract does not explicitly say that asymptomatic adults had only raised aldosterone.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) distinguished 2 forms of PHA I. One is a renal form, inherited as an autosomal dominant trait or occurring sporadically, in which salt wasting is limited to the kidney and improves with age. The other is a more severe, autosomal recessive multisystem form, in which mineralocorticoid resistance also affects the sweat glands, salivary glands and colon. The recessive form is caused by mutations in subunits of the epithelial sodium channel.

checks.claim: Hanukoglu (1991) distinguished 2 forms of PHA I.
checks.evidence_quote: type I PHA includes two clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects
checks.explanation: Two forms are distinguished.

checks.claim: Hanukoglu (1991) described a renal form of PHA I that is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait or occurs sporadically.
checks.evidence_quote: The pedigree was consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission with variable expression.
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant inheritance is supported; sporadic occurrence is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the renal form of PHA I described by Hanukoglu (1991), salt wasting is limited to the kidney.
checks.evidence_quote: two clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects
checks.explanation: The renal form is limited to the kidney.

checks.claim: In the renal form of PHA I described by Hanukoglu (1991), salt wasting improves with age.
checks.evidence_quote: Sodium supplementation was discontinued at the age of two.
checks.explanation: Improvement with age is implied by one case, not stated generally.

checks.claim: Hanukoglu (1991) described a more severe, autosomal recessive multisystem form of PHA I.
checks.evidence_quote: This pedigree was consistent with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance.
checks.explanation: The recessive kindred had severe, multiple-organ unresponsiveness and a recurrent life-threatening course.

checks.claim: In the autosomal recessive multisystem form of PHA I, mineralocorticoid resistance also affects the sweat glands, salivary glands and colon.
checks.evidence_quote: She had also increased salivary and sweat electrolytes consistent with PHA resulting from multiple organ unresponsiveness to mineralocorticoids.
checks.explanation: Sweat and salivary glands are mentioned; the colon is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of PHA I is caused by mutations in subunits of the epithelial sodium channel.
checks.explanation: Epithelial sodium channel mutations are not mentioned in this 1991 abstract.

paragraphs.text: Cheek and Perry (1958) are generally credited with the first description of pseudohypoaldosteronism: an infant with renal salt wasting who did not respond to mineralocorticoid.

checks.claim: Cheek and Perry (1958) are generally credited with the first description of pseudohypoaldosteronism.
checks.explanation: The title cannot show that this was the first description of pseudohypoaldosteronism. That historical credit comes from other sources.

checks.claim: Cheek and Perry (1958) described an infant with renal salt wasting who did not respond to mineralocorticoid.
checks.evidence_quote: A salt wasting syndrome in infancy.
checks.explanation: The title mentions a salt-wasting syndrome in infancy. It does not mention a single infant, renal origin, or lack of response to mineralocorticoid; any of these would be in the full text, which was not supplied.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) reviewed families with the renal form. Affected infants presented with salt wasting and failure to thrive. Their electrolytes became normal on salt supplementation, and with age they became clinically well. Clinically unaffected relatives often had raised plasma aldosterone, suggesting variable expressivity of a dominant trait.

checks.claim: Hanukoglu (1991) reviewed families with the renal form of PHA I.
checks.evidence_quote: We have studied two kindreds including a total of nine patients with PHA.
checks.explanation: One renal-form kindred was studied and the literature was analysed; 'reviewed families with the renal form' is only loosely supported.

checks.claim: In the families with renal PHA I reviewed by Hanukoglu (1991), affected infants presented with salt wasting.
checks.evidence_quote: the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy
checks.explanation: Salt wasting in infancy is reported.

checks.claim: In the families with renal PHA I reviewed by Hanukoglu (1991), affected infants presented with failure to thrive.
checks.evidence_quote: the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy (vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia)
checks.explanation: Failure to thrive is listed.

checks.claim: In the families with renal PHA I reviewed by Hanukoglu (1991), affected infants' electrolytes became normal on salt supplementation.
checks.evidence_quote: responded dramatically to a high salt diet (2.5 g/day)
checks.explanation: The patient responded to salt, but normalisation of electrolytes is not stated explicitly.

checks.claim: In the families with renal PHA I reviewed by Hanukoglu (1991), affected individuals became clinically well with age.
checks.evidence_quote: Sodium supplementation was discontinued at the age of two.
checks.explanation: Becoming clinically well is implied by stopping supplementation, not stated.

checks.claim: In the families with renal PHA I reviewed by Hanukoglu (1991), clinically unaffected relatives often had raised plasma aldosterone.
checks.evidence_quote: clinical expression of PHA varied from asymptomatic to moderate. In affected members (propositus, mother, and two brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr
checks.explanation: Asymptomatic expression and hyperaldosteronism are reported, but not specifically that clinically unaffected relatives often had raised aldosterone.

checks.claim: Raised plasma aldosterone in clinically unaffected relatives in renal PHA I families suggests variable expressivity of a dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: The pedigree was consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission with variable expression.
checks.explanation: The paper states dominant inheritance with variable expression.

paragraphs.text: The renal form of PHA I is transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait, and sporadic cases also occur. Clinical expression is variable: some heterozygous carriers have only biochemical abnormalities such as raised aldosterone.

checks.claim: The renal form of PHA I is transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: The pedigree was consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission with variable expression.
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant transmission is stated.

checks.claim: Sporadic cases of the renal form of PHA I occur.
checks.evidence_quote: Recently, in one sporadic and four dominant cases, four different mutations including two frame shift mutations, two premature termination codons, and one splice site mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) gene were identified.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions a sporadic case alongside dominant cases.

checks.claim: Clinical expression of the renal form of PHA I is variable.
checks.evidence_quote: clinical expression of PHA varied from asymptomatic to moderate
checks.explanation: Variable expression is stated.

checks.claim: Some heterozygous carriers of renal PHA I have only biochemical abnormalities such as raised aldosterone.
checks.evidence_quote: clinical expression of PHA varied from asymptomatic to moderate. In affected members (propositus, mother, and two brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr
checks.explanation: Asymptomatic affected members and hyperaldosteronism are reported; heterozygosity and 'only biochemical abnormalities' are not stated explicitly.

paragraphs.text: Geller et al. (1998) identified heterozygous mutations in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (NR3C2) in kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA I. The mutations included frameshift, premature termination and splice-site changes, consistent with loss of function and haploinsufficiency of the receptor. Within families the mutations segregated with the phenotype, including with raised aldosterone in clinically unaffected carriers.

checks.claim: Geller et al. (1998) identified heterozygous mutations in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene NR3C2 in kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA I.
checks.evidence_quote: have identified heterozygous mutations in one sporadic and four dominant kindreds
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 mutations identified by Geller et al. (1998) in autosomal dominant PHA I included frameshift, premature termination and splice-site changes.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two frameshift mutations (one a de novo mutation), two premature termination codons and one splice donor mutation.
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 mutations identified by Geller et al. (1998) are consistent with loss of function and haploinsufficiency of the mineralocorticoid receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two frameshift mutations (one a de novo mutation), two premature termination codons and one splice donor mutation.
checks.explanation: Truncating mutation types are consistent with loss of function, but the abstract does not explicitly mention loss of function or haploinsufficiency.

checks.claim: In the kindreds studied by Geller et al. (1998), the NR3C2 mutations segregated with the PHA I phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: These mutations segregate with PHA1 and are not found in unaffected subjects.
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: In the kindreds studied by Geller et al. (1998), the NR3C2 mutations segregated with raised aldosterone in clinically unaffected carriers.
checks.explanation: Abstract does not mention clinically unaffected carriers with raised aldosterone; it says mutations are not found in unaffected subjects.

paragraphs.text: Later studies found further heterozygous NR3C2 mutations, including missense mutations, in patients with the renal form of PHA I. Some of these mutations were de novo in sporadic cases. In some patients with the clinical phenotype, no NR3C2 mutation was found.

checks.claim: Studies after Geller et al. (1998) found further heterozygous NR3C2 mutations in patients with the renal form of PHA I.
checks.evidence_quote: PCR and direct sequencing of the MR gene identified a heterozygous point mutation changing codon 924 Leu (CTG) to CCG (Pro) (L924P) in all affected members.
checks.explanation: This 2000 study found another heterozygous MR mutation in a family with renal PHA1.

checks.claim: The further NR3C2 mutations found in renal PHA I included missense mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: To our knowledge, this is the first case of the missense mutation of the MR gene in renal PHA1.
checks.explanation: The paper reports the missense mutation L924P.

checks.claim: Some NR3C2 mutations in renal PHA I were de novo in sporadic cases.
checks.evidence_quote: In the sporadic case we identified a new frameshift mutation, Ins2871C, in exon 9 of the hMR gene. Family members were asymptomatic and had no mutation.
checks.explanation: The mutation was present in the sporadic patient and absent from the family members, which indicates a de novo mutation.

checks.claim: In some patients with the clinical phenotype of renal PHA I, no NR3C2 mutation was found.
checks.evidence_quote: In 2 kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA1 we found no mutation of the hMR gene.

paragraphs.text: Treatment is sodium chloride supplementation in infancy. Because mineralocorticoid sensitivity improves with age, supplementation can usually be tapered and stopped during childhood.

checks.claim: Treatment of autosomal dominant PHA I is sodium chloride supplementation in infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: responded dramatically to a high salt diet (2.5 g/day)
checks.explanation: Salt supplementation in infancy is reported for the dominant-form proband.

checks.claim: In autosomal dominant PHA I, mineralocorticoid sensitivity improves with age.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss mineralocorticoid sensitivity improving with age; it reports persistent hyperaldosteronism.

checks.claim: In autosomal dominant PHA I, sodium chloride supplementation can usually be tapered and stopped during childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Sodium supplementation was discontinued at the age of two.
checks.explanation: Stopping supplementation is shown in one patient; tapering and 'usually' are not stated.

paragraphs.text: Mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor developed severe salt wasting in the neonatal period, with hyperkalemia and markedly raised renin and aldosterone, and died without salt supplementation. This model resembles human PHA I.

checks.claim: Mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor developed severe salt wasting in the neonatal period.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 12 cited papers. The abstract does not mention mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor.

checks.claim: Mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor developed hyperkalemia.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 12 cited papers. The abstract does not mention mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor.

checks.claim: Mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor had markedly raised renin and aldosterone.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 12 cited papers. The abstract does not mention mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor.

checks.claim: Mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor died without salt supplementation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 12 cited papers. The abstract does not mention mice lacking the mineralocorticoid receptor.

checks.claim: The mineralocorticoid receptor knockout mouse model resembles human PHA I.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 12 cited papers. The abstract does not mention a mouse model.
